Hardening qualification, 2026-10-19

Source: vignettes/articles/contributor-tools-hardening-qualification.Rmd
contributor-tools-hardening-qualification.Rmd

Contributing · Object model · Discovery walkthrough · Object fields

Supporting record: claims apply to the revisions and environments named below; this page does not qualify a later candidate.

This is the preserved qualification of source 169c16e. The subsequent submission-diagnostic cleanup has a separate qualification report and archive identity; the receipts below are historical and have not been relabelled as checks of that newer source.

All ten recommendations are dispositioned in DISPOSITION.md. The implementation is frozen at 169c16e4ba00c687c1f03fe37e9d79a11d01cd8f. The later evidence commit changes only excluded tooling, CI and architecture documentation; it does not change the packaged implementation, tests or help. No push, merge, release or hosted workflow dispatch was performed here.

Exact final artifact

  • Archive: /private/tmp/sceptre-hardening-qualified-check/sceptre_0.99.0.tar.gz
  • SHA-256: fb6c3ad20da63c2d2595e08b54a8916e8eed9002e50fa62e877867718afa11b4
  • Built by default R CMD build source from a clean git archive of 169c16e; the build successfully created the vignette.
  • Source manifest verifies all 176 tracked R/native/help/test files byte for byte against that archive and records each SHA-256. Verifier is reproducible from the repository root. Final receipt edits leave all packaged source paths unchanged.
  • Build log, check log, 00check.log, installed suite, and BiocCheck log are terminal receipts.

The older f9f8142 provisional archive and the 8cbecfb archive under /private/tmp/sceptre-hardening-final-check/ are historical candidates. The latter had an unqualified slotNames() NOTE and advertised the rejected 3.1.7 floor. Neither is relabeled as this final artifact; their original paths remain intact.

Dependency floor and support

The retained R floor is R >= 4.1; the qualified test dependency is testthat >= 3.1.8. Both exact-source full suites use genuine, unmodified archived testthat3.1.8 in isolated libraries:

Runtime Cases Passes Failures / errors / warnings Explicit skips
R4.4.1, macOS arm64 253 5,505 0 / 0 / 0 10
R4.1.3, Linux arm64 Docker 253 5,505 0 / 0 / 0 10

Each lane reports 5,515 expectations including skips. The ten skips concern optional ondisc/backed behavior, because ondisc is absent in those environments; their names are recorded, not silently counted as passes. Imported-print mocking, 28 inventoried APIs/argument forms, and package/spec construction with R_DEFAULT_PACKAGES=NULL pass. The ordinary user libraries were not modified.

3.1.7 exports those APIs but fails the actual inherited-print mocking required by the sink error/interrupt tests on both R4.4 and R4.1. Those rejected-candidate logs remain labeled separately. Its unmodified source also cannot compile under R4.6 because of removed R internals; current-R checks use current testthat. No tests were weakened to retain an inaccurate floor. See dependency report, status, and provenance for exact image/archive/source hashes, full results and reproducible Docker/CI setup.

The standard OS jobs and pinned optional-backend job remain; R-devel, R-floor and official Bioconductor release/devel jobs are configured. Hosted runs were not executed. Local arm64 evidence does not establish Windows, x86, R-devel or Bioconductor-container success. The coherent 2024-03-01 CRAN snapshot makes the R4.1 dependency closure reproducible rather than resolving incompatible newest packages. CI regenerates the API inventory before probing, and the standalone probe regenerates a missing inventory; fresh-checkout and unknown-future-API probes are recorded in the dependency evidence.

BiocCheck and optional backend limits

BiocCheck1.47.26 on the final archive completed with 0 errors, 1 warning and 7 notes. The invocation disables the R-version and Bioc-help-subscription checks (no-check-R-ver, no-check-bioc-help); it is not an official submission acceptance. The warning is absence of a Bioconductor infrastructure dependency. An unused dependency was not introduced to hide it. The notes concern:

  1. Literal 1:3 output-level membership checks in the execution API.
  2. cat/print outside show methods, including intentional summary printing.
  3. paste in a condition signal.
  4. Three <<- sites.
  5. Function length.
  6. Missing runnable examples on the three experimental execution API help pages.
  7. Lines longer than 80 characters.

The API pages document the contracts and the real regressions exercise them; the example note remains unresolved. These are disclosed diagnostics, not a clean BiocCheck claim.

Local R4.6 tests qualify the installed ondisc1.2.0 interface/behavior; it has no RemoteSha, so its version is not a verified upstream source pin. Official upstream main/release inspection still found no supported public replacement for the required private count operations/shared-ID constructor. The lazy gate checks interface shape and native arities, not arbitrary future scientific behavior. ONDISC_CONTRACT.md records the exact inspected upstream commit, retained semantics, source-pin recommendation and external support/distribution gap. No new upstream-release/platform qualification or backed CRT support is claimed. Active backing files remain immutable; external content tamper monitoring is not introduced.

Performance and independent review

The bounded benchmark binds all 47 source/script hashes to 169c16e. Actual CRT output-level-three record ownership takes median 1.50ms (observed batch-average range 1.40–2.00ms), with 566,288 profiled R allocation bytes. A separate 500-row/128-arbitrary-draw synthetic graph is explicitly labeled. The tiny 160-source-cell/155-retained-cell, five-pair fixture has four response and two perturbation fit calls cold and zero of each warm, with exact result, fit and warning equality. Timings are comparable and noisy, so there is no speedup claim. Rprofmem measures R allocations, not peak/native memory. This does not qualify a large screen or arbitrarily large history.

Independent review used a clean installation of 8cbecfb and passed twelve focused checks verifying both reported collector fixes: conflicting valid warm fits reject atomically, and proposals no longer repeat full cell vectors. It also checked legitimate stale replacement and proposal ownership. See the preserved report and verification. The later narrow 169c16e review found the CI inventory omission and confirmed the explicit namespace/floor changes. The inventory fix is included in the evidence commit and owner-tested from a clean temporary checkout. The reviewer did not rerun its twelve checks or certify the final full suite/container/pipeline: this report does not upgrade that limited review into final cross-repository signoff.

The Nextflow adapter is maintained and qualified separately. Pipeline source, container image, scheduler, run/resume identity and direct/distributed parity must bind this exact package archive in that separate report. Package checks above do not establish Nextflow compatibility.
